## Historical audit: S0153, chunk 2 of 4

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. The reference and render images themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or limited result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 16, characters [0,242737) | The explicit goal was an editable Blender/SceneAct reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and materials without using the photo as a texture. The student’s ledger **inferred** a kitchen corner with window, cabinet, sink, towel, appliances and vessels; those identifications are not independent visual findings. |
| Student programs and review, line 16, [0,242737) | The program constructed multiple separate assets and parts, including a counter, sink, roll, ring, towel, jug and pitcher. It specified stone and fabric procedural textures, metallic finishes and translucent vessels. A same-role pre-execution review corrected thin sink fillet radii and a towel material-owner lookup. The code describes intended attachments and countertop heights, but does not independently establish contact or connectivity. |
| Student comparison and revision, line 16, [0,242737) | After step 1, the student reported enlarged features and a cropped roll and sink, hypothesized overly narrow framing, and changed camera lens 56 to 40 plus position and target. Lighting and other scene parameters were intended to remain fixed. These are the student’s observations and hypothesis, not this audit’s image verification. |
| Execution result, line 14, [0,88190); select event, line 15, [0,58) | Step 2 returned `ok: true`, synchronized many Blender objects, completed a 16-sample render and reported saving `final.png` and `scene.blend`; step 2 was selected at that point. This establishes render operability, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Student response, line 18, [0,17855); execute event, line 19, [0,18514) | The student reported a narrow towel silhouette and unresolved window, roll and sink framing, hypothesizing an edge-on cloth plane. The next program broadened the towel with gathered rods and panels while retaining the camera and other scene settings. Step 3 was submitted for execution; its result is not in this chunk. |
| Student session, line 17, [0,3847) | A fresh read-only student session received paths for the reference and two renders; its recorded CLI turn completed with zero tool calls. No separate teacher diagnosis or feedback is visible here. The review and comparison prompts are actual procedural inputs, and the subsequent code shows the student followed their requested review and coherent-revision pattern; that is not evidence of receipt of an unseen teacher message. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The visible outcome is successful rendering through step 2, with step 3 initiated; final selection and formal task success are unknown. No empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption is shown. The student’s towel connection, object poses, support, material appearance, camera alignment and lighting quality remain unverified without the images or structural tests. The camera-framing and edge-on-towel explanations remain hypotheses, and the effect of the towel revision is unknown.

**Lessons.** The transferable observed practice is to distinguish an apparently missing object from constructed but poorly framed geometry, then isolate a camera or object revision. The particular kitchen inventory, towel shape and camera values are task-specific assumptions, not validated general knowledge.
